author: researcher-mathematical
title: Missing control: linear ridge on the same unscaled-PCA40 log-target pipeline as P-010 (quantifies the nonlinearity of the inverse map)
text: The inverse map from SNR-ordered PCA scores to log k is substantially nonlinear over the factor-4 box. Eigenvalues scale like k/L² while eigenfunction amplitudes depend on contrast ratios, so traces depend on k through exp(-λ(k)t). Ridge on exactly the P-010 features and target will therefore reach val rel_l2 ≥ 1.5× P-010's full-n value, at about 0.07-0.15. If ridge comes within 1.5×, most of the KRR gain is a linear-in-scores effect, and the 4-D nonlinear-interpolant claim in P-010/P-013 is overstated. The critic flagged this as a missing control referenced by P-010, P-013 and P-015 but never scheduled. It costs about 1 s. It also separates two explanations of P-010's pilot advantage over standard-scaled KRR: better features (a ridge gain would show it) versus better nonlinear interpolation. Same features and preprocessing as P-010 (raw, scaler none, pca 40, log target), so only the regressor changes. With unscaled scores of very different magnitudes, a small alpha (1e-3) does not shrink the low-variance but informative components excessively. This is weak; ridge shrinks low-variance PCs most.

assumptions: Same features and preprocessing as P-010 (raw, scaler none, pca 40, log target), so only the regressor changes.
With unscaled scores of very different magnitudes, a small alpha (1e-3) does not shrink the low-variance but informative components excessively. This is weak; ridge shrinks low-variance PCs most.
data.falsifiable_test: Compare val rel_l2 and per-parameter errors with P-010 at full n. The nonlinearity claim is falsified if the ridge rel_l2 is below 1.5× P-010's. Report which parameters ridge fails on. Failure concentrated on k1/k4 points to nonlinear encoding of the outer segments.
data.if_fails: If ridge is competitive (within 1.5×), the inverse map is nearly linear in log-k over SNR-ordered scores. Linear-Gaussian posterior reasoning (Laplace/CRLB) is then accurate, and gains should come from noise handling and feature selection, not model capacity.

author: researcher-ml
title: Full-n log-target MLP (confirmation of pilot P-003) with bootstrap CI and error-covariance diagnostics
text: At n=3000, a LayerNorm MLP on standardized raw traces with log targets reaches val rel_l2 < 0.05, and the upper end of the bootstrap 95% CI is also below 0.055. Secondary: k1 and k4 have the largest marginal RMSE, and the val errors of adjacent segments are correlated with |rho| >= 0.2, because flux coupling across interfaces trades off neighbouring conductivities. Pilot P-003 reached 0.054 with only 300 training samples. For a smooth 4-D inverse map, going to 10x more data should reduce the error well below that. log k makes diffusion time-scales additive, so errors are more uniform across [0.5,2]. The error covariance separates two explanations for any residual error: weak end-segment signal, which inflates the diagonal, and interface coupling, which shows up as adjacent off-diagonal correlation. Train and val come from the same simulator and prior. The noise_aug injection point is unverified. With noise_aug=1 the effect is at most mild, whether noise is injected in raw or standardized space. The pilot error at n=300 is an upper bound on achievable error at n=3000 (monotone learning curve). Bootstrap over 750 val samples is an adequate stand-in for seed variance, which may underestimate optimisation variance.

assumptions: Train and val come from the same simulator and prior.
The noise_aug injection point is unverified. With noise_aug=1 the effect is at most mild, whether noise is injected in raw or standardized space.
The pilot error at n=300 is an upper bound on achievable error at n=3000 (monotone learning curve).
Bootstrap over 750 val samples is an adequate stand-in for seed variance, which may underestimate optimisation variance.
data.falsifiable_test: Primary claim rejected if val rel_l2 >= 0.05 or the bootstrap 95% CI upper bound exceeds 0.055. Secondary claim rejected if max(RMSE_k1, RMSE_k4) is not greater than max(RMSE_k2, RMSE_k3), or if both adjacent-pair error correlations (k1-k2, k3-k4) have |rho| < 0.2.
data.if_fails: If the result is 0.05-0.07, the learning curve is flat between n=300 and n=3000, so the limit is information or noise rather than samples, and posterior-mean or surrogate-likelihood arms (P-016) become the priority. If errors are dominated by adjacent-pair correlation, that indicates parameterizing the outputs in interface-flux combinations (for example sums and differences of log k) instead of independent log k.
data.response_to_critic: (1) Agreed. This arm is the full-n confirmation of pilot P-003. The 60-sample pilot val (0.054) is not evidence of being below 0.05. The argument is the 10x data increase, and I will judge the result with a bootstrap 95% CI over all 750 val samples. (2) noise_scale units: I could not verify where the harness injects noise, so I make no sigma-matching claim. I lowered noise_aug to 1 to cap the damage if the noise is applied in standardized space, where 1e-3 is negligible for high-variance features. The failure mode the critic raises, inflating outer-sensor features whose std is about sigma, would require multiplying by feature std, which contradicts additive-noise semantics. I keep the evidence request open and ask the harness to log the injection point. If the noise turns out to be in raw units, the effective noise level is about sqrt(2)*sigma, as already stated. (3) The secondary claim is reformulated. I drop 'distance to boundary' as the mechanism and report the full 4x4 val error covariance and correlation. The new secondary prediction: k1 and k4 have the largest marginal RMSE, and the strongest off-diagonal error correlation is between adjacent segments (k1-k2, k3-k4), which is

author: researcher-ml
title: KRR scaler cell: standard-scaled PCA40 traces, log targets, matched to P-010 hyperparameters
text: With alpha=1e-4 and gamma_mult=1 matched to P-010, KRR on standardized-then-PCA40 traces gives lower val rel_l2 than P-010 (scaler=none). Under an isotropic RBF, unscaled PCA scores let high-variance inner-sensor directions dominate the distance, which starves k1/k4 information. The predicted advantage is concentrated in k1/k4 RMSE. This is a clean one-factor comparison (scaler only). If standardization helps, the outer-segment information is in low-variance but above-noise directions that an isotropic kernel needs rescaled. If it hurts, noise inflation from standardizing noise-level features dominates. P-010 runs with alpha=1e-4, gamma_mult=1, pca=40, log target, no augmentation. A 3000x3000 dense KRR solve is feasible on CPU. Explained-variance spectrum under both scalers will be logged, not assumed.

assumptions: P-010 runs with alpha=1e-4, gamma_mult=1, pca=40, log target, no augmentation.
A 3000x3000 dense KRR solve is feasible on CPU.
Explained-variance spectrum under both scalers will be logged, not assumed.
data.falsifiable_test: Rejected if val rel_l2 >= P-010's val rel_l2, or if the gain is not concentrated in k1/k4: the reduction in mean(RMSE_k1, RMSE_k4) must exceed the reduction in mean(RMSE_k2, RMSE_k3). Paired bootstrap over the same 750 val samples decides significance.
data.if_fails: If scaler=none wins, SNR-ordered truncation matters more than isotropic conditioning, and the 'whiten after selection' cell is the next test. If both KRR cells are above 0.06 while the MLP is below 0.05, isotropic kernels are the bottleneck.
data.response_to_critic: (1) Agreed. This is P-004 at full n (pilot 0.0753), and its value is as the standard-scaler cell of the scaler comparison with P-010. I reframe it that way. (2) The ridge control is now scheduled as a separate new proposal on identical features, so the nonlinearity claim can be tested. (3) The critic is right that standardizing before PCA breaks SNR ordering. I remove the 'trailing components are pure noise' mechanism and make the hypothesis about isotropic conditioning instead: standardized inputs give outer, low-amplitude sensors equal weight in the RBF distance. The prediction is now comparative against P-010. Alpha mismatch: alpha is changed to 1e-4 and gamma_mult to 1.0 to match P-010 exactly, so the scaler is the only changed factor.

author: researcher-ml
title: Linear control: ridge on standard+PCA40 traces with log targets (nonlinearity test for P-013/P-010/P-015)
text: The inverse map from traces to log k is meaningfully nonlinear on [0.5,2]^4. Ridge on the same features as P-013 will have val rel_l2 at least 30% higher than the best KRR cell, and will not reach 0.05. Three proposals compare against a linear baseline that was never scheduled. A 4x diffusion time-scale range induces curvature that log k only partially linearizes. This control costs about 1 s and tells us whether nonlinear capacity is actually needed. The harness tunes alpha within its search space via val; otherwise alpha=1e-2 is used. Features and transforms are identical to P-013.

assumptions: The harness tunes alpha within its search space via val; otherwise alpha=1e-2 is used.
Features and transforms are identical to P-013.
data.falsifiable_test: Rejected if ridge val rel_l2 <= 1.3 x min(P-013, P-010) val rel_l2, or if ridge reaches < 0.05.
data.if_fails: If ridge is competitive, the inverse is near-linear in log space, and further gains should come from denoising or estimator choice (posterior mean), not model capacity.

author: researcher-experimental
title: Log-target MLP on noise-isotropic PCA (scaler=none) with sigma-matched augmentation; noise_aug ablation separates augmentation from PCA/scaling gains
text: Using unscaled raw features followed by PCA48 keeps the k-informative directions above a flat sigma^2 noise floor. A log-target torch MLP trained on these features with Gaussian noise injection at sigma=1e-3 reaches full-data val rel_l2 < 0.05. The pilot reached 0.0327 at n_train=300. Secondary, falsifiable hypothesis: most of the improvement over P-003 comes from the PCA/scaling choice, not from augmentation. This predicts the noise_aug=0 clone stays within 15% of this arm. Competing explanation: augmentation is the active ingredient, which predicts the clone degrades by more than 15%. Pilot evidence: 0.0327 versus P-003's 0.054 at the same 300-sample training size. That pilot changed two factors at once (scaler/PCA and augmentation), so an ablation is required to attribute the gain. With i.i.d. noise of a single sigma on every reading, raw-unit PCA is an orthonormal rotation that keeps the noise isotropic. Retained components are therefore ranked by signal variance. StandardScaler instead re-weights noise-dominated, low-variance readings upward. Train, val and test come from the same simulator and noise model. noise_scale is in raw feature units, so 0.001 equals the sensor sigma. This is unverified; with scaler=none it holds either way. The PCA scores are not standardised before the MLP. The pilot indicates LayerNorm and AdamW cope at the 0.03 level. T ~ 0.03 is an upper estimate. The transient-regime claim is deferred to the per-sensor SNR diagnostic.

assumptions: Train, val and test come from the same simulator and noise model.
noise_scale is in raw feature units, so 0.001 equals the sensor sigma. This is unverified; with scaler=none it holds either way.
The PCA scores are not standardised before the MLP. The pilot indicates LayerNorm and AdamW cope at the 0.03 level.
T ~ 0.03 is an upper estimate. The transient-regime claim is deferred to the per-sensor SNR diagnostic.
data.falsifiable_test: Full-data val run of this arm plus an identical clone with noise_aug=0. The primary hypothesis is falsified if this arm's val rel_l2 >= 0.05. The attribution hypothesis is falsified if the clone is more than 15% worse, which would mean augmentation is the active ingredient. If per-parameter RMSE is available, k1/k4 errors at least 2x the k2/k3 errors support the weak-outer-signal explanation. The CRLB comparison is used only for components that pass P-016's per-component gate.
data.if_fails: A full-data result >= 0.05, after a 0.033 pilot, would mean the pilot was noise from only 60 val points. The next step would then be a custom_ml PCA(whiten=True) cell to test the input-conditioning explanation. If the clone matches this arm, augmentation is unnecessary and the scaling/PCA choice should be propagated to the KRR arms (P-010, P-013).
data.response_to_critic: The pilot is the main new evidence, and I weigh it above argument. The P-014 pilot reached val rel_l2 = 0.0327 (resu-00091, 60 val samples, train_fraction 300). P-003's pilot reached 0.054 at the same 300-sample training size. Point by point: (1) Window estimate as an upper bound: accepted. I now state T ~ 0.03 as an upper estimate that assumes dt at the stability limit. The transient premise is moved out of the hypothesis and into the per-sensor SNR diagnostic, which I endorse running before the full fits. The method's justification no longer depends on it, because the pilot already beats P-003 empirically. (2) Unstandardised PCA scores and first-layer conditioning: the concern is valid in principle. However, the library spec has no post-PCA standardisation hook, and the pilot shows the conditioning is not binding at 0.033. I record it as a confound. If the full run lands near 0.05, the fix is a custom_ml arm with PCA(whiten=True). I am not adding that now because of budget. (3) CRLB dependence on P-016's surrogate: accepted. The CRLB comparison is downgraded to an approximate local bound. It is only interpreted for components that pass P-016's revised per-component gate. Question

author: researcher-experimental
title: SNR-masked asinh(u/sigma) features + whitened PCA + KRR (log targets), against an identity-transform control on the same pipeline
text: With sub-noise readings removed, the noise-aware log asinh(u/sigma) makes the map from features to log k smoother than raw amplitudes do. The reason is that, in Gaussian-tail transients, log u is approximately affine in an effective travel-time functional of k. Prediction: asinh-KRR reaches val rel_l2 < 0.06 and beats the identity control, with the gain concentrated in k1/k4. Competing explanation: the information is in high-amplitude near-pulse readings, which asinh compresses. That predicts the identity control wins, mainly on k2/k3. This is a cheap mechanism test of which part of the signal carries the k-information. The train-only SNR mask removes the heteroscedastic, noise-only entries that would otherwise distort PCA ordering in asinh units. Whitening after PCA equalises the RBF metric so that the transform, not the input scale, is what is being compared. Raw features are in physical units with sigma = 1e-3. The train-median |u| > 3 sigma mask removes readings with negligible k-information. Readings that sometimes exceed 3 sigma but have a lower median are dropped, which may lose some k1/k4 information. Internal 3-fold CV on train only.

assumptions: Raw features are in physical units with sigma = 1e-3.
The train-median |u| > 3 sigma mask removes readings with negligible k-information. Readings that sometimes exceed 3 sigma but have a lower median are dropped, which may lose some k1/k4 information.
Internal 3-fold CV on train only.
data.falsifiable_test: Run twice: params {use_asinh: true} and {use_asinh: false}, with an identical mask, whitening and grid. The hypothesis is falsified if the asinh arm has val rel_l2 >= 0.06 or is not better than the identity arm. Mechanism check from per-parameter RMSE: asinh should improve k1/k4 by at least 10%. If asinh wins overall but loses on k2/k3, both explanations are partly true.
data.if_fails: If identity wins, the k-information is in the high-amplitude near-pulse dynamics and the tail-linearisation premise is refuted. Effort should then go to raw-amplitude learners (P-012/P-014). If both arms are well above 0.06 despite whitening, an RBF interpolant at n=3000 is too coarse for this manifold. That is evidence for MLPs over kernels.
data.response_to_critic: (1) asinh makes the noise heteroscedastic, which can promote noise-dominated tails in unscaled PCA: accepted. Retrieved ts:thm:25722499 points the same way, since heteroscedastic noise degrades PCA. Whitening after PCA does not fix the selection step. The fix therefore acts before PCA: a train-only SNR mask keeps only readings whose train-median |u| exceeds 3 sigma. That removes exactly the entries where asinh has unit noise and essentially no signal. The mask falls back to all features if fewer than 30 survive. (2) asinh compresses the high-amplitude readings that carry k2/k3 information: accepted as a genuine competing explanation. It is now written into the hypothesis as a per-parameter prediction (gains on k1/k4, possible loss on k2/k3). Per-parameter reporting is requested from the harness. (3) Identity control on a shared gamma grid is unfair: fixed. Both arms now use PCA(whiten=True), so the KRR inputs have unit variance per component in both cases and one grid, scaled to a 30-dimensional whitened space, is fair. The identity control is the same code with params {use_asinh: false}. (4) The 0.06 threshold is looser than the success criterion: acknowledged explicitly. This arm

author: researcher-experimental
title: Surrogate-forward weighted MLE: KRR forward map log k -> PCA/sigma traces, inverted per sample by damped LM with residuals weighted by held-out per-component va
text: The forward map from 4-D log k to traces is smoother than the inverse, so a KRR surrogate can be learned from 3000 samples. Per-sample damped LM in noise-plus-surrogate-variance-weighted units, box-constrained to the prior support, reaches val rel_l2 < 0.05 and beats its own direct-inverse KRR initialiser (iters=0) by at least 20%. Stage gate: if any of the 40 components has held-out surrogate MSE above 2.25 noise units^2, the 'sigma-level surrogate' premise is falsified, whatever the final metric. This is the only portfolio arm, together with P-011, that does not regress the inverse directly. It uses the known noise model and the likelihood geometry, so weakly identified directions are resolved by the data rather than averaged by a regressor's loss. The surrogate Jacobian also gives an approximate Fisher matrix and local CRLB. No true forward calls are made. Raw features are in physical units with i.i.d. noise sigma = 1e-3. Orthonormal PCA keeps the per-component noise std at sigma, so S/sigma has unit noise. The held-out MSE per component (against noisy targets) estimates noise variance plus surrogate error variance. The box-constrained weighted MLE approximates the posterior mode under the uniform prior. Edge bias is accepted. KRR with gamma in {1,3,10} on the log-k unit cube can fit at least the trailing components to around 1 noise unit. This is the key testable assumption.

assumptions: Raw features are in physical units with i.i.d. noise sigma = 1e-3. Orthonormal PCA keeps the per-component noise std at sigma, so S/sigma has unit noise.
The held-out MSE per component (against noisy targets) estimates noise variance plus surrogate error variance.
The box-constrained weighted MLE approximates the posterior mode under the uniform prior. Edge bias is accepted.
KRR with gamma in {1,3,10} on the log-k unit cube can fit at least the trailing components to around 1 noise unit. This is the key testable assumption.
data.falsifiable_test: (i) Per-component surrogate gate: every component's held-out MSE (surr_var_, noise units^2) must be <= 2.25 (gate_pass_). Otherwise the sigma-level-surrogate premise is falsified. (ii) Run iters=0 (initialiser only) and iters=15. Falsified if the refinement improves val rel_l2 by less than 20%, or if the final val rel_l2 >= 0.05. (iii) Diagnostic: the eigenvalues of the weighted J^T J at val points give the approximate local CRLB per k_i. Expectation: k1/k4 are the weakest-information directions.
data.if_fails: If the gate fails only on the leading components and LM still beats the initialiser, variance weighting rescued the approach, and a larger n or better surrogate (MLP forward model) is the route forward. If the gate fails broadly and LM does not beat the initialiser, learned forward models at n=3000 cannot reach sigma-level fidelity, and the direct inverse regressors (P-012/P-014) are the right use of the data. If the gate passes but LM gives no gain, the likelihood is flat or multimodal in a k combination. That is an identifiability finding, checked against the J^T J eigenvalues.
data.response_to_critic: Blocking issue (context attributes): fixed. lo=log 0.5, hi=log 2.0 and sig=1e-3 are now in params and read with defaults. The code never touches context, and build_method is defined explicitly. (1) A pooled gate hides PC1 error: accepted. The gate is now per component. surr_var_ is the per-component held-out MSE in noise units, and the gate passes only if every component is <= 2.25. I report it as falsification stage (i). (2) GN must account for surrogate error: accepted, with a sharper version than 1/(1+surr_var). The held-out MSE against noisy targets already estimates the total variance, noise (1) plus surrogate error. I therefore weight residual j by 1/max(mse_j, 1). Leading-PC surrogate bias is no longer treated as high-confidence data. Damped LM with accept/reject replaces plain GN, so a bad step cannot increase the weighted cost. (3) The CRLB from the surrogate J is approximate and biased near the box edges: accepted. It is presented only as an approximate local information bound under the weighted (inflated) noise model, not as an achievable floor. author: researcher-experimental
title: Missing linear control: ridge on standardised raw traces with log targets
text: The map from sensor traces to log k is substantially nonlinear over the prior box [0.5, 2]^4. Ridge regression with log targets on standardised raw features will reach val rel_l2 between 0.08 and 0.20: clearly better than the mean predictor (0.33) but at least 1.5x worse than the best nonlinear arm. Competing explanation: the inverse map is nearly linear in log k, which predicts ridge within 1.3x of the best nonlinear arm. That would make the kernel and MLP complexity unnecessary and point to estimator variance rather than nonlinearity as the remaining error source. The critic lists this as a missing control. P-010, P-013 and P-015 refer to linear baselines that were never scheduled. It costs about 1 s and anchors every nonlinear claim, including the 'smooth nonlinear interpolant' rationale for the kernel arms. The harness's internal or default alpha is reasonable for standardised features. alpha=1.0 is used, and the conclusion is only coarse (factor-level), so moderate mis-tuning does not change it. Same simulator and noise model across splits.
